entries.note: He describes difficulty envisioning further progress, without specifying a predicted capability limit.

entries.test: Public deployment records showing whether the discussed restaurant ordering systems could perform the intended workers' complete jobs without human assistance at publication.
entries.note: The wording preserves his qualified assessment of existing systems.
The normalization drops the claim that LLM outputs all look and sound alike. The overall comparison of value is subjective, although paid rewriting work is separately checkable.
He explicitly says full replacement is very unlikely.
Calling Covello optimistic does not specify an alternative outcome or deadline.
Making him eat crow or making the investment worth it supplies no shared standard for judging a release.
The claim concerns what faster execution can cause. Intelligence, sentience and consciousness lack a shared test in this formulation.
The central claim judges whether the technology's benefits justify its costs.

entries.test: Google's published emissions inventories and explanations of emissions growth would establish the five-year increase and generative AI's contribution.
entries.note: Changing 'chasing' to 'while it chased' weakens the implied causal attribution to coincidence. The judgments about search quality and returns are not settled by emissions figures.

entries.test: Public records of an AI investment collapse would show whether successive setbacks culminated in a major failure such as a leading AI company's collapse.
entries.note: 'I think the collapse will' expresses a firm forecast; Character.ai is an example, not a required failure.

entries.test: Public reporting or investor disclosures would establish a setback prompting a venture firm to push an AI startup sale, or the sudden collapse of a major AI company.
entries.note: Either alternative can satisfy the prediction; no deadline is stated.

entries.test: Public financial disclosures showing sustained profitability at OpenAI or Anthropic from continued generative AI development would contradict the asserted absence of a path to profitability.
entries.note: The claim extends beyond current losses to the viability of continued generative AI development.
'It's unclear how' expresses doubt about survival, not a firm prediction that the companies will fail.

entries.test: Public financial results would test current unprofitability, while controlled capability studies could test whether probabilistic generation produces the asserted inherent limitations.
entries.note: This combines financial observations with an explicit causal explanation. 'Unsustainable' is less precise than the profitability component.
The overall claim judges whether costs and power use are justified. 'Isn't getting cheaper' could be checked separately against historical costs.

entries.test: Public adoption, retention and commercial-use evidence for generative AI applications available or demonstrably forthcoming at publication would establish whether any had compelling mass-market utility.
entries.note: 'Killer app' has a plain commercial reading as an application that drives substantial adoption.
This is an explicit judgment of worth.
